item.title: [MED] Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
item.description: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today's epic patch batch dwarfs September's record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.

item.title: [LOW] Anthropic Warns Small AI Models Could Soon Form Self-Propagating IoT Botnets
item.description: Small artificial intelligence (AI) models may be months away from developing capabilities to self-replicate on IoT devices like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes, according to a warning from Anthropic. item.title: [LOW] Docker Fixes Critical Two-Year-Old Hub Flaw That Let One User Push Images as Another
item.description: A flaw in Docker Hub, the registry where container images are published and downloaded, let one user push, pull, or delete images as another user. Docker fixed the flaw on September 30 and says it found no evidence that anyone exploited it. The flaw was in the feature that converts a personal account into an organization, Docker said in a security advisory on October 12.

item.title: [LOW] GoBalance Flaw Lets Attackers Hijack .onion Addresses by Recovering Tor-Format Keys
item.description: A bug in GoBalance, a tool many dark-web sites use to stay reachable during attacks, lets anyone work out the secret key that controls a site's .onion address using only public information, and then take that address over. Searchlight Cyber, which disclosed the flaw on October 8, says an attacker who recovers the key can redirect the site's visitors to a copy of the site they control.
